description: This case study is the final report of the National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling, titled Deep Water: The Gulf Oil Disaster and the Future of Offshore Drilling and delivered to the US President in January 2011. Its 398 pages follow the disaster in three parts: the path to the tragedy, including the history of offshore oil and gas and the regulation of Gulf deepwater production, then the causes and consequences, covering the Macondo well and blowout, response and containment, environmental impacts and recovery, and finally lessons for industry, government and energy policy. The foreword records eleven crew deaths and more than four million barrels of oil released into the Gulf after the explosion on 20 April 2010. Access: free PDF download from the US Government Publishing Office; no licence is stated and it is a federal publication. Coverage is the Gulf of Mexico and US offshore regulation. Caveats: it is a narrative investigation with few tabulated data, and only the foreword and contents were read here. It suits emergency response and resilience studies of offshore oil systems, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
